text:
Vasily Podkolzin went 10th overall in 2019 and spent years as a useful depth winger. This season he looks like something more, and the question is how much more. He has 12 goals and 19 points in 23 games, eight of them on the power play, where he's now on the ice for 44% of Edmonton's chances after 12% last season. On Tuesday in Florida he had two goals and an assist in a 5-2 win.

Some of it is real. His own chances are up to 1.21 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.78, the Oilers take 61% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him out there, and he still plays heavy (70 hits). He ranks 23rd in the league in wins added by his goals.

Some of it isn't. He's shooting 26% against 14% last season, with 12 goals on 8.0 expected, and Edmonton has scored 11.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Finishing like that rarely holds. Also worth watching: his ice time over the last ten games is down to 15:26. Even so, our projection has him around 28 goals, which would be a career year by a distance.
headline: Podkolzin's breakout is real, mostly
